title: Computed GOTO — GOTO (10, 20, 30) K branches by 1-based index into a label list
sourceContent:
SUBROUTINE PROCESS_OP(OPCODE, V)
C     Computed GOTO: branches to label_K when OPCODE = K. When
C     OPCODE is outside [1..3], control falls through to the
C     statement IMMEDIATELY AFTER the GOTO (silent default). Most
C     modern languages refuse silent fall-through; the spec must
C     capture both the branch table and the fall-through semantic.
      IMPLICIT NONE
      INTEGER OPCODE
      REAL    V
      GOTO (10, 20, 30) OPCODE
C     <-- silent default lands here when OPCODE NOT in [1,3]
      V = -1.0
      RETURN
   10 V = 1.0
      RETURN
   20 V = 2.0
      RETURN
   30 V = 3.0
      RETURN
      END
notes: Computed GOTO is a F77 idiom for dispatch tables. A Java/C# switch statement is the natural port, but the spec MUST capture the silent-default fall-through. Many migrations 'fix' this by raising an exception on unknown opcodes — that's a behavioural change requiring SME sign-off.
